project.title: Muster — The Agentic Fire Drill
project.audience: WebMCP Challenge judges and safety-training facilitators
project.promise: Rehearse a changing building incident on one visible, reviewable command surface.

promptEditableManifest.editPolicy: Change manifest fields before changing component timing or layout code.

missingAccess: Observed native WebMCP discovery in a compatible browser

productAnalysis.audience: Fire-safety drill facilitators and WebMCP judges
productAnalysis.problem: Plans, occupants, roles, injects, decisions, and review evidence become fragmented during a rehearsal.
productAnalysis.solution: A visible fictional drill state shared by a human facilitator and bounded page tools.
technicalSignals: One manager and eighteen bounded page tools

viewerContext.assumedKnowledge: The viewer has not seen Muster and may not know WebMCP.

productNouns.inject: a controlled change introduced during a drill
productNouns.fixture register: fictional aggregate occupant counts used for training
productNouns.runtime trace: a visible receipt of what each page tool did
productNouns.Incident Commander: the manager that routes a request to bounded specialists

templateStrategy.selectionMode: Ranked by immediate proof, safety-boundary clarity, and judge readability.
templateStrategy.selectedReason: The strongest story is the visible workflow and its human authority boundary, not a generated metaphor.

proofInventory.claim: The app presents an orbitable 18-floor building, guided workflow, trace, and conversation surface together.
The inspectable Floor 07 plan, drawn route, changed exit, and staged review are visible in the same interface.
A single real browser take advances the visible rehearsal and stops before human approval.
A fictional responder has a visible role, location, task, authority boundary, and page-only movement control.
One manager exposes four specialist lanes and nineteen inspectable page-tool contracts.
The staged report preserves scope, objective, plan basis, route evidence, actions, open gaps, and human approval.
Five hundred shuffled workflows preserve state and approval boundaries.
A compatible browser discovers the page tools natively.

timingPlan.rhythm: human why → team problem → live request → visible change → mechanism → trace → authority boundary → proof ledger → CTA
timingPlan.microBeatPolicy: No artificial dead-air holds; every beat either advances the request or gives the viewer one readable fact.
timingPlan.proofHoldPolicy: Human context opens the film; real product proof and reconstructed product interactions remain clearly distinguished.
timingPlan.captionPolicy: Primary overlays stay below eight words and outside the product-reading region.

screenPlan.reason: Begin with why missing decisions matter before an emergency.
Show the whole command surface before explaining technology.
Run one continuous guided rehearsal and stop before approval.
Make the persistent sketch receipt and boundary readable.
Tie the route to a fictional responder and named responsibility.
Connect the human request to specialists, tools, state, and trace.
Make input, output, why, visible change, and guardrail readable.
Make the human-only approval boundary unmistakable.
Separate working and tested proof from pending native discovery.
Show the actual manager and page-tool browser.
End product proof on the reviewable report and approval control.
End on one action and the training boundary.

architecture.title: One request becomes a visible plan
architecture.authorityBoundary: The agent prepares; the human confirms observations and approves.

threePlan.reason: The native CSS 3D building selects the loaded floor, then hands off to a pan-and-zoom plan where room inspection and route drawing change the agent workflow.

scenes.headline: A fire exposes every missing decision.
scenes.support: An unavailable exit. Two people needing help. A role nobody owns yet.
scenes.narration: In an emergency, there is no time to discover an exit changed or an assistance role has no owner. Teams need to rehearse those decisions together.
scenes.intelligenceRole: The changed condition creates a coordination problem the agent must help the facilitator resolve.

scenes.headline: Rehearse before conditions change.
scenes.support: Controlled scenario. Shared plan. Human authority.
scenes.intelligenceRole: The first divider turns urgency into a concrete preparation task.

scenes.headline: The plan becomes a shared rehearsal.
scenes.support: Building, people, scenario, decisions, and evidence stay on one screen.
scenes.narration: The facilitator gets one command room for the plan, fictional occupants, response roles, scripted changes, and review evidence.
scenes.intelligenceRole: The whole product is visible before any architecture explanation.

scenes.headline: One guided rehearsal, captured live.
scenes.support: Every visible change waits for the facilitator.
scenes.narration: This is one real page take. The facilitator selects Floor Seven and advances one declared tool at a time. The plan is read before the scenario starts. The Studio is inspected, Stair B becomes unavailable, exits are compared, and the decision is recorded. Nothing auto-completes the exercise or contacts a building system.
scenes.intelligenceRole: The agent begins from the same visible and revisioned context as the facilitator.

scenes.headline: The plan changed.
scenes.support: Now the team must respond to the same visible condition.
scenes.intelligenceRole: The divider marks the moment the authored scenario creates a decision.

scenes.headline: A sketch becomes reviewable evidence.
scenes.support: Length · endpoint · scripted availability · human-review boundary
scenes.narration: The facilitator draws a path. The page measures it, checks its endpoint against the scenario's exit status, and keeps the result visible without calling it a real evacuation route.
scenes.transitionOut: route lines fan into specialist connections
scenes.intelligenceRole: A visible scenario change requires route comparison and named responsibility, not generic chat.

scenes.headline: A route still needs an owner.
scenes.support: Fictional role · current position · task · authority boundary
scenes.narration: The people layer makes responsibility visible. Each fictional responder has a role, exercise position, task, and boundary. The facilitator records only confirmed actions.
scenes.intelligenceRole: Role ownership turns a route suggestion into a coordinated rehearsal action.

scenes.headline: Every call leaves a trace.
scenes.support: Input, result, purpose, visible change, and guardrail.
scenes.intelligenceRole: The divider moves from spatial work to inspectable agent behavior.

scenes.headline: One manager. Four bounded specialists.
scenes.support: Named page tools read or update one deterministic in-page state.
scenes.narration: A human request enters the Incident Commander, which routes to plan, people, equipment, or review specialists. Named page tools read or update one deterministic state. The interface changes, the trace records the result, and the human controls the final decision.
scenes.transitionOut: tool nodes collapse into visible receipts
scenes.intelligenceRole: This makes the manager-specialist-tool hierarchy legible without overstating autonomy.

scenes.headline: The runtime explains its own work.
scenes.support: Selected call · input · output · why · screen change · boundary
scenes.narration: Select any call to see its input, output, purpose, visible page change, duration, and guardrail. Open gaps remain visible instead of being silently resolved.
scenes.intelligenceRole: The agent's activity is inspectable in the same product surface.

scenes.headline: The agent prepares. The human decides.
scenes.support: Report approval is not a page tool.
scenes.narration: The agent prepares. The human decides.
scenes.intelligenceRole: The authority divider makes the final control boundary unmistakable.

scenes.headline: A draft is not an approval.
scenes.support: Scope, actions, route evidence, and open gaps remain reviewable.
scenes.narration: When every problem has an owner, the agent stages an after-action draft. A Fire Safety Manager reviews the evidence and uses the separate human approval control.
scenes.intelligenceRole: The system is useful because it coordinates evidence while preserving human accountability.

scenes.headline: Proof stays separate from promise.
scenes.support: Working interface. Tested contracts. Explicit remaining gate.
scenes.narration: Five hundred shuffled workflows test transitions, repeat-safe actions, route boundaries, and human approval. Native discovery still needs a compatible-browser recording.
scenes.intelligenceRole: The video distinguishes tested contracts from an unobserved browser capability.

scenes.headline: Bounded tools, visible consequences.
scenes.support: No alarms, dispatch, doors, sensors, or autonomous approval.
scenes.narration: Every tool has clear limits and visible consequences.
scenes.intelligenceRole: The divider introduces the declared tool surface and its limits.

scenes.headline: Nineteen contracts. One visible state.
scenes.support: One manager plus eighteen bounded page tools.
scenes.narration: One manager and eighteen page tools expose purpose, example input, visible effect, and safety boundary before the fixture can be run.
scenes.intelligenceRole: The real contract browser makes the WebMCP surface inspectable rather than magical.

scenes.headline: The result stays reviewable.
scenes.support: Training evidence only · human authority retained
scenes.narration: The result is a reviewable training record, not a safety certification.
scenes.intelligenceRole: The final product proof shows the evidence package and approval control together.

scenes.headline: Run the drill before the fire.
scenes.support: Fictional table-top training · Not for live emergencies
scenes.narration: This is fictional table-top training software. Try the live drill.
scenes.intelligenceRole: One clear next action follows an honest proof boundary.

audio.policy: AI narration generated from the approved script with GPT Realtime 2.1 using the Marin voice. It is not a human firefighter recording.

knownLimitations: All people counts, locations, equipment, timestamps, and incidents are fictional training fixtures.
The product does not connect to alarms, dispatch, responders, doors, sensors, or live building systems.
The agent cannot infer participant intent or competence; final report approval is human-only.
Native WebMCP discovery was not observed in the available test browser; the current evidence is source contracts, local tests, and the manual product surface.
The narration is AI-generated from the approved script and is not a human firefighter recording.
